observed_vs_expected: The best_target_score rose from 0.5346 to 0.8458 over six rounds, contradicting the early-stabilization expectation under the strict periodic hypothesis. Valid candidates decreased to 9, slightly below the expected >10 threshold but safely above the critical floor. Thicknesses failed to converge to the predicted quarter-wave windows (90-100 nm HfO2, 130-140 nm SiO2); instead, low-index layers clustered tightly between 59.0-65.0 nm, while high-index layers exhibited extreme variance (115.0-254.0 nm) without settling.
deviation_mechanism: The divergence stems from material dispersion and finite-period phase accumulation. At 375 nm, HfO2's refractive index drops sufficiently via Sellmeier dispersion that strict quarter-wave physical thickness shifts lower to maintain optical path balance, pushing the optimizer toward ~115 nm rather than 90-100 nm. Simultaneously, SiO2 layers locked near 60 nm because the system prioritized minimizing dispersion-induced sidelobes over maintaining identical quarter-wave optical thickness. High-index layers beyond the central 8 periods show weak field sensitivity, causing the optimizer to treat them as unconstrained impedance-matching stubs rather than structural components, resulting in the observed outlier spread.
continue_rationale: The latest round yielded a gain of 0.003635 (from 0.8422 to 0.8458), which exceeds the reference epsilon of 0.0001, confirming substantive rather than numerical convergence. Valid candidates remain at 9, well above the stop-trigger threshold of 5. With only 6 rounds executed, the schedule has not approached hard limits, and the unexplored thickness basin suggests further optimization can bridge the remaining gap to the theoretical optimum.
insight_for_next: Force a deliberate probe of the expected quarter-wave region by resetting all high-index layer initializations to 95.0 nm while locking low-index layers at the empirically stable 60.0 nm. Pair this with a tightened optimizer step-size (e.g., halve the learning rate) to prevent the solver from drifting into insensitive outer-region optima and to encourage convergence within the constrained physical band.
insight_grounding: Current measurements show candidate 3 (latest iteration) low-index layers stabilizing at 60.0 nm, 59.0 nm, and 59.0 nm across positions 1, 3, and 9, confirming physical robustness in that regime. Conversely, high-index layers span 115.0 nm (position 0) to 254.0 nm (position 18) with extreme outliers like 25.0 nm at position 23, directly demonstrating the optimizer's abandonment of the 90-100 nm target without systematic testing. The score delta of 0.0036 from round 5 validates that the landscape remains navigable with adjusted initialization.
